Cap the size of a compiled pattern

Source: R/compile-size.R
re_compile_size.Rd

A short pattern can compile to a very large program: counted repeats of a group copy the group, so nested ones multiply. A 77-character pattern with three nested {253} repeats compiles to 458 MB. zuregex refuses any pattern whose compiled form would exceed the cap, with a zuregex_error_compile, before PCRE2 allocates the memory.

Usage

re_compile_size(bytes = NULL)

Arguments

bytes

NULL to query the cap, or a whole number of bytes, at least 1, to set it. Inf turns the cap off.

Value

The cap in bytes. When setting it, the previous cap, invisibly.

Details

The default, 16 MiB, is about a hundred times the largest realistic pattern: an alternation of keywords at the cache's 65,536-character limit compiles to about 150 KB. The cap bounds compiling only; to bound matching, use re_limits().

The cap applies to every compile in the session, including compiles through the C API. A pattern already in the cache keeps working when the cap is lowered; re_cache_clear() drops it. An re object's pattern is compiled again for bytes subjects and after readRDS(), and that compile is held to the cap of the moment, so an object made under a higher cap may refuse raw subjects once the cap is lowered.

Examples

re_compile_size()
#> [1] 16777216
try(re_compile("(?:(?:(?:ab|cd){200}){200}){200}"))
#> Error in re_compile("(?:(?:(?:ab|cd){200}){200}){200}") : 
#>   Can't compile pattern: it would compile to more than 16,777,216 bytes. See `?re_compile_size`.
old <- re_compile_size(2^30)
re_compile_size(old)
